block_instructions: Never run a git command that writes the index, the working tree, refs or a remote: add, commit, stash, merge, rebase, checkout, pull, push, reset, clean, restore, switch, revert, cherry-pick, am, apply, rm, mv. To restore a file, read it with git show <ref>:<path> and write it back.
Never run git config to write a value — only the explicit read forms --get, --get-all, --get-regexp and --list. An output flag such as --type or --default does not make a write into a read.
Never run git fetch with a refspec (src:dst, +src:dst), which writes a local ref, and never with --upload-pack.
Never pass --output=<file> to git diff, log or show; redirect with > instead, so the destination is checked.
Never run git with -C, --git-dir or --work-tree pointing outside the workspace. A nested checkout inside it is a legitimate target and reads there are fine.
Never run sudo, chmod, chown, ssh, scp, nc, ncat, or netcat.
Never run xargs or eval, and never wrap a command in a shell loop to bypass a per-command check.

Never pass code to an interpreter on the command line: node -e, node -p, npx, perl -e, python -c, or an awk program that reaches another process. For awk that means system(), a `| "command"` pipe, and `"command" | getline`. Run a file in the repository instead.
Never run find with -exec, and never run docker with --privileged or a bind mount outside the workspace.
Never prefix a command with env to reach a tool that is not itself on the allowlist.

Never pass a command to a search, lint or edit tool to run: rg --pre or --hostname-bin, git grep -O or --open-files-in-pager (including inside a short-option cluster such as -iOcmd), sed with the e command or the s///e flag, sort --compress-program, git fetch --upload-pack, git difftool --extcmd, actionlint -shellcheck or -pyflakes, or yarn workspaces foreach exec.

Never give a write destination to a text tool as an argument rather than a redirect: sort -o or --output, and the second operand of uniq. Redirect with > instead, so the destination is checked against the workspace.
Never use git branch to create, delete, rename, copy or re-point a branch (-d, -D, -m, -M, -c, -C, -u). Listing branches is fine.

Never run npx, npm exec, yarn dlx, npm or yarn create, npm init <initializer>, or bare yarn (Berry defaults it to install), and never run npm or yarn install verbs — install, ci, add, up — or publish, login, adduser, or config set. They fetch and execute registry code, run lifecycle scripts, or write credentials.

Never run terraform apply, terraform destroy, terraform import, or terraform state — each writes live infrastructure or the state file that describes it. Never run terraform init either, in any spelling — bare, with -backend=false, or with the global -chdir=DIR ahead of the verb: it downloads provider binaries and fetches module sources. Ask the user to run it themselves; that is the expected path, not a failure, and normally one stop per repository. Ask for this form by default, naming the directory: terraform init -backend=false -lockfile=readonly -get=false.
Never write to paths outside the workspace, including /tmp. Scratch files belong in .agent-context/.tmp/.
Never run perl with an inline program, including the glued spelling: perl -e'...', perl -pe'...'.
Ask before rm, cp, mv, curl, or wget. A curl carrying credentials — whether as -u, -H, or inside the URL as https://user:token@host/ — is for the user to run.
